newsitem.title: GERMANY: Bonn sells Alpine hotel to save money for EMU.
newsitem.headline: Bonn sells Alpine hotel to save money for EMU.

text.p: In another show of Finance Minister Theo Waigel's determination to qualify for Europe's single currency, a German army resort home in Davos, Switzerland came under the hammer on Thursday.

But despite hard times for Bonn, Germany's fighting men and women will not lose access to the hotel built in 1908 on the outskirts of Davos which the Bundeswehr has used for recreational purposes since 1967.

The Finance Ministry said it sold the government's stake in Mon Repos Erholungsheim Davos AG, whose only holding is the hotel in Davos Village, to the Bundeswehr's social services organisation for 8.7 million marks.
"This sale brings the government's privatisation concept another step forward," it said in a statement.
